findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the extracted heartbeat-alert and binding-drift-alert subcommands read DRY_RUN and short-circuit all rebar writes when it is 'true' (the gate that lives in the current steps' YAML `if:`), and add a dry-run unit case asserting zero rebar mutating calls.
evidence: Workflow lines 215/223-226/261-264/279-282/336/346-349/383-386/398-401: every find/open/comment/close step is gated by `env.DRY_RUN == 'false'` — the dry-run gate is control flow that lives in the YAML `if:` today.
dry_run is a first-class workflow_dispatch input (lines 32-40) whose stated contract is 'Report staleness without creating/closing tickets'.

Plan subcommand descriptions ('find existing open alert by marker tag, open when stale+none, comment when still stale, close on recovery — one function per transition') and Testing ('no-op paths') never name DRY_RUN, so the branch that today lives in YAML `if:` may be dropped when the steps collapse into one subcommand.
findings.finding: The plan collapses the heartbeat/binding-drift find/open/comment/close steps — currently gated by YAML `if:` conditions that include the DRY_RUN=='false' mutation gate — into single per-family subcommands, but the subcommand contracts never state that DRY_RUN must be read and honored inside Python. If the extracted heartbeat-alert / binding-drift-alert functions omit the dry-run gate, a workflow_dispatch with dry_run=true will create/comment/close real alert tickets, silently breaking the documented 'Report staleness without creating/closing tickets' contract.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (heartbeat-alert / binding-drift-alert subcommands); Scope; Testing (Unit)
scenarios: An operator triggers the canary via workflow_dispatch with dry_run=true to check staleness; the collapsed heartbeat-alert subcommand, missing the DRY_RUN guard, opens/comments/closes real bug tickets.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass DRY_RUN via env into the alert subcommands; have each transition function return a planned action and only invoke the rebar runner when DRY_RUN != 'true'. Add unit tests: dry_run=true → find may run but open/comment/close issue no rebar create/comment/transition.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Note explicitly that the canary's step-invocation changes are exercised only post-merge (parity via workflow_dispatch) and are not gated by the pre-merge Verified run — i.e. the f1eb executes-from-main trap does not apply here — so no transitional shim is needed.
evidence: Ticket f1eb comment (Patchset 1 Verified-1): 'gerrit-verify.yaml executes from MAIN's workflow definition against the patchset tree — a change that deletes the shell probe can never pass main's still-shell golden-path step … 4th consumer class beyond the 3 enumerated in-tree ones.'

The canary (reconcile-bridge-canary.yml) is schedule/workflow_dispatch-only and is not invoked by test.yml or gerrit-verify's suite, so the executes-from-main trap does NOT actually apply to it — but the plan states no such reasoning, and its parity step is post-merge workflow_dispatch (AC5), so an in-session pre-merge exercise of the new invocations is not claimed.
findings.finding: The plan does not reason about whether re-pointing the canary's workflow STEPS to `python scripts/canary_bridge.py <subcommand>` clears the pre-merge Verified gate, a dimension that just bit the immediately-preceding sibling port. In f1eb, gerrit-verify.yaml was found to execute the workflow-step definition from MAIN against the patchset tree, so a change that re-points a golden-path step to a not-yet-present script path failed the gate and required a transitional shim.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (Thin YAML re-point); Testing (Parity: workflow_dispatch post-merge)
scenarios: A reviewer expects the new canary invocations to be exercised by the pre-merge gate and is surprised they are not, or a later maintainer copying this pattern to a gated workflow re-hits f1eb's failure.

findings.finding: The plan proposes extracting the reconcile-bridge push-retry loop to a Python entry point, but the codebase already made and test-enforced the OPPOSITE decision: that this block must drive the workflow YAML directly and be tested verbatim, precisely because extraction 'would introduce a drift seam where the workflow's invocation of it becomes untested glue.'
findings.location: Approach / Scope (reconcile-bridge run blocks -> thin invocations)
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the Scope so the push-retry/commit-back loop stays in YAML (keeping its verbatim-execution test), and target extraction at the canary's classification/alert-filing blocks and any expression-free helpers only; state explicitly why those differ from the push loop.

findings.finding: The claim that the reconcile-bridge raw git commit 'routes through the canonical write seam' is mechanism-underspecified: that step commits the reconciler's uncommitted event files plus its own binding-store commit and pushes a whole dirty worktree, which does not match the per-ticket append_event/write_and_push seam signature, and the seam's own code warns that a whole-index commit there races normal store writes.
findings.location: Approach ('the raw git commit site routes through the canonical write seam') / AC line 2

findings.finding: The push-retry/merge/backoff logic the plan proposes to migrate into 'tested Python' already has a canonical Python implementation (src/rebar/_store/push.py::push_tickets_branch), AND the workflow's copy deliberately diverges from it in ways a prior closed bug (4c4f) recorded as intentional — so a straight extraction/routing-through-the-seam would regress a documented decision rather than de-duplicate.
findings.location: Approach + Scope + Acceptance Criteria line 1 ('Workflow run-blocks reduced to env + single-command invocations; logic lives in tested Python')

findings.finding: AC-2 says the reconcile-bridge raw git write should be 'routed through the canonical seam,' but the commit it targets writes the RECONCILER's pre-materialized inbound event files — a path the codebase explicitly documents as a separate writer that must NOT be conflated with the general local write seam (event_append.write_and_push). The plan names no specific seam and does not address this boundary.
findings.location: Approach ('the raw git commit site routes through the canonical write seam') + Acceptance Criteria line 2 ('The reconcile-bridge raw git write is routed through the canonical seam')

findings.finding: Migrating the reconcile-bridge push/merge retry loop is a behavioral hunk that directly reverses a recently completion-verified design decision (ticket 4c4f) to keep that loop in YAML and test it verbatim; the plan neither classifies this hunk against that decision nor acknowledges it.
findings.location: Approach: 'move workflow run-block logic into Python entry points' + Scope 'run blocks -> thin invocations'

findings.finding: The plan proposes extracting the reconcile-bridge run-blocks (including the push-retry loop) to Python without engaging existing repo prior art that explicitly argues AGAINST that extraction.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'Alternatives / prior art' note addressing test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py's rationale: explain how the migration avoids the untested-glue drift seam (e.g. by keeping the thin YAML invocation itself under the bridge smoke suite and pinning arg/env plumbing), and confirm the bug-cited invariants (e161 pipefail classification, 4c4f no-backoff CAS, explicit refspec, merge-not-rebase I1) are preserved with equivalent unit tests. If the retry loop is genuinely better left as verbatim YAML, scope it out and migrate only the classification/alert-filing logic.

findings.finding: The plan does not enumerate the test consumers outside .github/workflows/ that assert directly on the shell run-block TEXT of the two workflows and would break when run-blocks are thinned to Python invocations.
findings.location: Scope: '.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml + canary workflow: run blocks -> thin invocations'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Scope subsection listing these five tests and, for each, whether the invariant it guards (merge-not-rebase, fetch-depth:0, explicit refspec, --class-on-close, blobless pack guard) is re-asserted against the migrated Python or against the surviving thin YAML step.
